plainLanguage: Section 129 — Uttering word with intent to wound religious feelings. Kifungu hiki ni sehemu ya ulinzi wa worship, religious assemblies, burial places, funeral rites au religious feelings kulingana na statutory wording yake.
meaning: Liability under section 129 depends on the exact prohibited conduct and the intention, knowledge, voluntariness or lawful-authority qualification expressly stated in the provision.
keyPoints: Analyse the exact statutory conduct, not merely the heading.
Prove the required mental element where intention, knowledge, voluntariness or wilfulness is specified.
Respect any lawful-authority qualification and the precise penalty stated by the section.

cases.name: Hamisi Rajabu Dibagula v Republic
cases.relevance: The appeal concerned section 129 and the requirement of deliberate intention to wound religious feelings.

history.summary: Section 129 appears in Chapter XIV — Offences Relating to Religion and Burials — Penal Code [CAP. 16 R.E. 2022].
notes: Official text verified against the government-hosted R.E. 2022 Penal Code.

expertPerspectives.label: Mtazamo A
expertPerspectives.view: Intention, knowledge, voluntariness or wilfulness should be proved where the statutory text expressly requires it.

expertPerspectives.label: Mtazamo B
expertPerspectives.view: The conduct, assembly, place, remains or religious feelings involved must fall within the actual wording of the section.

debateQuestion: Je, facts na evidence zinatimiza kila statutory element ya section 129?
disclaimer: Ufafanuzi huu si maandishi rasmi ya sheria.
